item.title: German state elections deal a blow to Chancellor Friedrich Merz
item.description:
Reps. Ro Khanna (D-Calif.) and Thomas Massie (R-Ky. ) announced Thursday they've secured commitments for the 218 signatures needed to force another vote the release of files related to sex offender Jeffrey Epstein . The big picture: Answers about the disgraced financier and his web of wealthy connections have continued to haunt the administration, with Attorney General Todd Blanche now facing the threat of contempt proceedings over the Epstein files. This is the bipartisan duo's second push in less than a year after they forced their first Epstein transparency bill through Congress, which the president signed after initially opposing the effort. item.title: Germany's Merz vows to press ahead with reforms after historic state election defeat
item.description:
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz on Sunday described his CDU party's heavy losses in two regional elections as a "disaster", but vowed to push ahead with a reform drive. The far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) party took first place in the northeastern state of Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, exit polls showed, and also gained in strength in another election in Berlin.

item.title: Iran-backed Houthi rebels warn against joining Saudi Arabia in Yemen's growing civil war
item.description:
Saudi Arabia said Saturday that its air defenses destroyed a ballistic missile fired by Yemen’s Houthi rebels at Riyadh, the first strike on the Saudi fighting with the Iran-backed group reignited this summer. The Saudi-led coalition confirmed the interception hours after the dawn launch. Residents reported hearing an explosion, and journalists saw firefighters extinguish a blaze on the Aramco-branded fuel tank at a depot near King Khalid International Airport. No casualties were reported. Coalition spokesman Turki al-Maliki said the Houthis also tried to hit civilian infrastructure in Yanbu — the Red Sea terminus of a key Saudi oil pipeline — as well as Taif, Baysh and Farasan, all of which were thwarted. item.description:

item.title: Evenepoel wins fourth world time trial title in a row, Reusser retains her crown
item.description:
Cor Vos A year after making even Tadej Pogačar look distinctly ordinary on the hilly Rwandan time trial course, Remco Evenepoel demolished all around him once again in Montréal, winning his fourth-consecutive time trial world title by almost a minute over former world champion Filippo Ganna. Evenepoel set the best time at all three time checks throughout the 39.2-kilometre course, but another rider who impressed, and who spent a short stint in the hotseat at the end of the afternoon, was 19-year-old Paul Seixas. The young Frenchman has proved before that he's a jolly decent time trialist, but on a power-specialist course like that of Montréal, Seixas put in one of the rides of the day to ultimately finish third – young Swede Jakob Söderqvist had looked on track for a podium finish but a late crash bumped him to fifth.
